traits.notes: The seedling displays a distinct whorled leaf arrangement at the apex. Some leaves exhibit minor damage, including small holes and margin notches.

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves, approximately 8 to 10, are clearly attached at the same terminal node forming a rosette-like cluster)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are crowded at the shoot apex)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade attached to the stem)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins appear smooth, though some minor mechanical damage is visible on a few leaves)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaves are widest near the base and taper to a point)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (leaves taper to a distinct, elongated tip)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (leaves taper gradually toward the petiole attachment)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib is visible with secondary veins branching off it)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible (secondary veins are clearly visible, running parallel to each other from the midrib toward the margin)
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (the leaf surface reflects light, indicating a glossy texture)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on the leaf surface)
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are present but appear short relative to the leaf blade length)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear cylindrical and rounded in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (the stem appears stiff, lignified, and brown, characteristic of a tree seedling)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the visible portion of the stem appears hairless)
    19.	Stem color: brown (the stem is brownish in color)
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stem surface appears relatively smooth without prominent ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are clearly visible at the leaf attachment points)
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex is visible)
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen pulvinus joint is visible at the base of the leaf petioles)
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are present)
F. Notes: The seedling displays a distinct whorled leaf arrangement at the apex. Some leaves exhibit minor damage, including small holes and margin notches.
